item.title: China slams U.S. espionage against Chinese enterprises
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
China slams U.S. espionage against Chinese enterprises BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Commerce on Friday voiced "grave concerns" and "firm opposition" over a U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) official's remarks on taking Chinese enterprises as allegedly legitimate targets for espionage, urging an immediate cessation of such activities. "The U.S. side's brazen claims that Chinese enterprises are legitimate targets for espionage have thoroughly ripped off the fig leaf behind which intelligence agencies covertly steal secrets, exposing the bandit logic of hegemony in broad daylight," a ministry spokesperson said. China solemnly urges the U.S. side to immediately cease all espionage activities against China, including against Chinese enterprises, and to stop all actions that undermine China's sovereignty, security and development interests, said the spokesperson. China possesses "the firm will and ample means" to resolutely take necessary measures in accordance with laws and regulations, such as the Counter-Espionage Law, to severely punish illegal and criminal acts and firmly safeguard the legitimate and lawful rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, according to the spokesperson. The comments came after CIA Deputy Director Michael Ellis recently stated that the United States is engaging in a broader range of espionage against China including Chinese enterprises, claiming that Chinese firms in areas such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors and biotechnology are legitimate targets of such activities. The U.S. moves to overstretch the concept of national security, blur the boundaries between competition and security, and even frame economic competition as a so-called "threat" are essentially driven by the zero-sum, Cold War mentality, the spokesperson said. "U.S. intelligence agencies' acts to interfere with normal economic competition severely damage the expectations of businesses worldwide and sabotage the global market environment for fair competition," the spokesperson stated. While the U.S. side has long accused its trading partners of harming its interests through intelligence theft, U.S. intelligence agencies have engaged in large-scale cyber espionage and intelligence theft around the world. Now, they flagrantly violate international trade rules and intellectual property protection norms by targeting economic competitors through espionage activities, the spokesperson noted, criticizing the U.S. side for applying double standards. Refuting U.S. claims that China poses military and economic threats as "a bandit's rhetoric that inverts black and white" and "malicious slander," the spokesperson called the U.S. acts as suppression and smearing against China. "China's technological breakthroughs in fields such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors, and biotechnology are the fruits of the dedicated efforts of Chinese researchers and enterprises, by no means prey to be arbitrarily coveted by U.S. intelligence agencies," the spokesperson said. Noting U.S. anxiety over China's technological progress, the spokesperson stated that espionage and hegemonic suppression cannot halt the innovative strides of Chinese enterprises, nor can they win genuine technological leadership. item.title: Commentary: BRICS opens up new possibilities for more dynamic Global South
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
Commentary: BRICS opens up new possibilities for more dynamic Global South An aerial drone photo taken on June 17, 2022 shows the headquarters building of the New Development Bank (NDB) in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Fang Zhe) BEIJING, Sept. 12 (Xinhua) -- When the BRICS cooperation mechanism was formally launched in 2006, it opened a new chapter for cooperation among major emerging economies. Two decades on, BRICS has, through the ebbs and flows of the global economy, expanded through multiple rounds of enlargement and broadened the scope of its cooperation. This evolution has ushered in a new era of greater BRICS cooperation, better reflecting the growing weight and aspirations of the Global South. When BRICS leaders prepare to gather for this year's summit in New Delhi, India, the mechanism is playing a greater role in amplifying the collective voice of emerging economies, and expanding practical cooperation amid a changing international landscape beset by raging protectionism and economic fragmentation. Its growing weight is reflected in its economic and demographic scale. BRICS countries now account for approximately 40 percent of global GDP at purchasing power parity and nearly half of the world's population. Data released by the UN Trade and Development in March showed that the intra-BRICS merchandise trade has expanded more than 13-fold since 2003, and exports reached 1.17 trillion U.S. dollars in 2024. BRICS, however, is more than an economic force. Its growing significance lies in how countries with different development paths are pooling their strengths in resources, industry and technology to advance shared development. A prominent area is financing. For many developing economies, access to affordable, long-term funding remains critical to turning development ambitions into reality. The New Development Bank (NDB), headquartered in Shanghai, has helped provide such an option by mobilizing resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects. Figures released by the bank showed that by the end of the first quarter of 2026, the NDB had approved 42.9 billion dollars in financing for 140 projects. Covering such areas as infrastructure, clean energy and digital transformation, these projects address the pressing development needs of Global South countries while echoing the priorities highlighted by the theme of the forthcoming BRICS Summit, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability." The ever-evolving BRICS cooperation is also helping developing countries gain new growth momentum. In recent years, BRICS cooperation has been expanding into areas like renewable energy, digital infrastructure, scientific and technological innovation. Photo taken on Aug. 24, 2017 shows a flowerbed at the Xiamen International Conference and Exhibition Center in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province. (Xinhua/Jiang Kehong) A case in point is the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center in Xiamen, which was established in 2020 to provide a platform for cooperation in digitalization, advanced manufacturing and technological innovation. These efforts point to the broader value of BRICS: it is not simply giving the Global South a stronger voice, but creating practical opportunities for countries to access financing, technology and cooperation suited to their development needs. Such collaboration helps explain BRICS' growing appeal to countries seeking greater opportunities to participate and cooperate. As a founding member, China has contributed not only by building platforms for practical cooperation, but also by supporting greater openness and broader participation to promote high-quality cooperation within an expanded BRICS. Some in the West portray BRICS as a rival bloc seeking to build a parallel order. Yet this claim bears little resemblance to reality. BRICS stands for openness, inclusiveness and mutual benefit, not confrontation or exclusion. That is fundamentally different from the exclusive blocs championed by some Western countries, and a key reason behind the growing vitality of BRICS. Looking ahead, BRICS is poised to embark on its third "golden decade" after 20 years of growth and transformation. By rising up to the challenges of the times, BRICS countries can help shape a more equal and orderly multipolar world and a more universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and, in doing so, write a new chapter of solidarity and cooperation across the Global South. item.title: China, India are making arrangements for Xi-Modi meeting, says spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
China, India are making arrangements for Xi-Modi meeting, says spokesperson BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China and India are making arrangements for a meeting between President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the upcoming 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Friday. This will mark the third consecutive year in which Xi and Modi meet, following their meetings in Kazan and Tianjin, said Mao Ning, the spokesperson, at a regular news briefing. She said China stands ready to work with India to follow the strategic guidance of the two leaders, view bilateral relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, strengthen communication, expand cooperation, and properly handle differences, so as to be good-neighborly friends and partners helping each other succeed. item.title: Xi's "development first" vision spurs Global South's shared growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
Xi's "development first" vision spurs Global South's shared growth Chinese expert Li Guiqiang (L) gives instructions on vegetable cultivation at the China-Ethiopia Addis Ababa Agricultural Technology Demonstration and Training Center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on Aug. 20, 2025. (Xinhua/Han Xu) BEIJING, Sept. 12 (Xinhua) -- At the SCO summit last week, Chinese President Xi Jinping called on countries to "stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity." Amid a turbulent and rapidly changing international landscape, development still faces severe challenges, and the road to prosperity for the Global South will not be straight. "The Global South emerges for development and prospers through development. We should make ourselves the main driving force for common development," Xi said during the 2024 BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia. For Xi, development has always been a priority. He sees it as "the master key to solving all problems," and has consistently called for countries worldwide to jointly pursue development and prosperity. Xi has stressed repeatedly that no one should be left behind in the fight against poverty in China, and has led a formidable campaign that ended extreme poverty nationwide, which was hailed as "the greatest anti-poverty achievement in history." His "leaving-no-one-behind" conviction also extends to his efforts to support poverty reduction and spur development across the Global South. "On the path to modernization, no one, and no country, should be left behind," Xi said. Last week in Bishkek, Xi called for consolidating cooperation in both traditional and emerging fields, from trade, investment, connectivity and energy to artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy and green industries. An aerial photo taken on Oct. 22, 2025 shows wind turbines of De Aar Wind Power Project in De Aar, Northern Cape, South Africa. (Xinhua/Han Xu) Responding to the Global South's aspirations for common development and modernization, Xi has proposed the Global Development Initiative (GDI), which marks its fifth anniversary this year. In the last five years, the GDI has mobilized more than 23 billion U.S. dollars, provided support for over 1,800 "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, and sponsored training programs for more than 200,000 people in different professions. Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper, said: "Under Xi's leadership, the concept of development has acquired a new international dimension and become part of a broader vision for humanity's shared future." Established in 2023, the Key Laboratory of Ancient Chinese Script, Culture Relics and Artificial Intelligence of Jilin University brings together researchers in the fields of paleography, archaeology, history, artificial intelligence, etc. With oracle bone inscriptions, bronze inscriptions, Warring States scripts, and Qin and Han scripts as core subjects for research, the laboratory sorts and catalogs scripts and culture relics in a systematic manner, and facilitates its work with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. item.title: Multinationals bank on new opportunities as China upgrades services sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
Multinationals bank on new opportunities as China upgrades services sector * The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services, running from Sept. 9 to 13, has attracted a heavier presence of multinational companies compared to last year, with 473 of these being either Fortune Global 500 firms or industry leaders. * China has actively promoted trade in services and opened its services sector wider. These efforts are creating more opportunities for countries and businesses around the world. * By bringing together governments, international organizations and investors, the fair provides a unique opportunity for exchange, sharing of experiences, and the creation of opportunities. BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Opportunities, partnerships and shared prosperity are among the most frequently mentioned terms by exhibitors and guest speakers who are in Beijing for a major services trade fair. This was evident when Ragnhild Sjoner Syrstad, Norway's state secretary for industry and commerce, briefed a large crowd at the Norwegian Pavilion on her nation's exhibition at the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS). As the guest country of honor for this year's event, Norway has brought firms spanning health, nutrition, design and lifestyle to its pavilion. According to Syrstad, the stronger presence and diversity of Norwegian firms demonstrate the importance Norway places on both the CIFTIS and the business relationship between the two countries. People visit the booth of Norway, the guest country of honor for the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS), in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Photo by Lin Qiujin/Xinhua) Another example was Alexander Poulev, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister and minister of economy, investment and industry, who explained why his delegation has traveled more than 7,000 km to attend the CIFTIS. He praised the fair as an opportunity to turn the longstanding friendship between Bulgaria and China into concrete investments, stronger trade, and long-term economic cooperation. With the theme of "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," this year's CIFTIS features the debut of over 100 new products and services, covering fields such as information and communications, fintech, and digital and intelligent healthcare. A series of forums and business matchmaking activities are also being held. EXPLORE OPPORTUNITIES The 2026 CIFTIS, running from Sept. 9 to 13, has attracted a heavier presence of multinational companies compared to last year, with 473 of these being either Fortune Global 500 firms or industry leaders. During the fair, U.S. pharmaceutical giant Lilly, a Fortune Global 500 company, is showcasing innovative treatment solutions across the fields of metabolic diseases, neuroscience, oncology and immunology. Wang Li, head of Lilly China's drug development and medical affairs center, said that as China's clinical research capabilities and innovation ecosystem have continued to advance, the country has become an indispensable partner in Lilly's global R&D system. In 2024, Lilly established a medical innovation center in Beijing, focusing on enhancing clinical development efficiency, accelerating new drug R&D and implementing medical solutions. In 2025, the firm launched its first overseas innovation incubator, Lilly Gateway Labs, also located in Beijing. Wang said the Lilly innovation incubator not only brings Lilly's expertise in science, management and resource support to local startups but also deeply integrates into Beijing's pharmaceutical industry ecosystem. Visitors walk past the booth of Lilly during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS), in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Ma Ping) Banking on China's huge medical market demand, the company announced earlier this year that it planned to invest 3 billion U.S. dollars in China over the coming decade to expand supply-chain production capacity. This decision marked another significant move by the company to deepen its roots in China and support the development of the local healthcare industry. "We will use the CIFTIS as a bridge to actively introduce global innovation into China, and collaborate with top local academic and industrial forces to bring more innovative treatment options to patients, jointly promoting the high-quality development of China's pharmaceutical and health industry," Wang noted. ABB, a global leader in electrification and automation technologies and also a Fortune Global 500 company, is eyeing the vast business potential arising from China's urban renewal. Lars Eckerlein, general manager of ABB China Limited, said China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) opens a new chapter for the nation's real estate and construction sectors. He added that the company is proud to leverage its expertise in construction and renovation to support China's urban renewal and its sustainability and high-quality development goals. Speaking about his firm's participation in projects across China, from renovating aging buildings to improving energy efficiency, Eckerlein said the Shekou Tower renovation in Shenzhen in south China had achieved an energy-saving rate of 75 percent and cut carbon emissions by 142 tonnes annually. The project also helped remove potential hazards posed by outdated facilities, using an integrated energy management solution. Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said China has actively promoted trade in services and opened its services sector wider. These efforts are creating more opportunities for countries and businesses around the world, he said in a keynote speech delivered at the 2026 Global Trade in Services Summit that marked the opening of the fair. China runs a deficit in services trade, with its imports growing steadily. The value of annual services imports has stood at around 4.4 trillion yuan (about 650 billion U.S. dollars) per year in recent years. Visitors communicate with each other during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xin) BUILD PARTNERSHIPS As the first national-level comprehensive services trade exhibition in the opening year of China's 15th Five-Year Plan, the CIFTIS not only injects fresh vitality into global services trade, investment and consumption, but also serves as a platform for promoting openness and cooperation among countries and fostering mutually beneficial partnerships. Poulev, the Bulgarian deputy prime minister, said trade in services is an important pillar of bilateral ties. "We want to see more organic products reaching the Chinese market and more Bulgarian companies building long-term partnerships with Chinese businesses." He also said that Chinese companies have globally competitive technologies in sectors like electric mobility, software, automation, robotics and advanced manufacturing, while Bulgaria has skilled engineers and an established industrial ecosystem. "This creates a strong opportunity that combines Chinese technology and investment with Bulgarian engineering and expertise," he said, adding that Bulgaria also offers a strategic location for companies looking to expand their presence in Europe. In Poulev's view, stronger investment cooperation can create new supply chains and enhance the value of bilateral trade. "We are ready to build the next generation of Bulgaria-China economic cooperation together." People visit the booth of Bulgaria during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Pan Xu) This willingness to build stronger partnerships resonates with the African region. In a video address to the summit, Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye, who also serves as the current chairperson of the African Union, said that the CIFTIS, as one of the world's largest platforms for trade in services, embodies a vision of openness, cooperation and shared development. By bringing together governments, international organizations and investors, this fair provides a unique opportunity for exchange, sharing of experiences, and the creation of opportunities, he said. "In a constantly changing world, we need more than ever to move forward together, share our experiences, and innovate to create new opportunities and build a better future for our countries," he said, adding that efforts should be doubled to turn trade in services into a true driver of shared prosperity, sustainable growth and economic development. People visit the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Han) PROMOTE PROSPERITY Ding, the Chinese vice premier, pointed out that trade in services is an important component of international trade and is playing an increasingly important role in driving global economic growth and industrial upgrading. He said that amid the accelerating restructuring of the international economic and trade landscape, advancing trade in services and promoting opening up and cooperation in the services sector is not only China's choice but also a necessity for the world. Johanna Hill, deputy director-general of the World Trade Organization (WTO), told the summit in a video address that services account for around half of global trade in value-added terms. This share is only likely to grow, propelled by the rise of digital technologies, notably AI. At the same time, services are becoming an ever more important part of global supply chains. They support not only production, but also design, management, logistics and distribution. Johanna Hill, deputy director-general of the World Trade Organization (WTO), delivers a video address during the Global Trade in Services Summit of the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Xiaoyu) Against the background of complex and sometimes frail international trade relations, she said countries that have successfully integrated services trade in their development strategies can share their experience and support those that are still making the transition. Hill also said that China is already helping translate its experience into practical support via cooperation with the WTO. The South-South capacity building program, additionally, provides an important vehicle for doing this, by supporting developing countries in areas such as services trade, investment facilitation and electronic commerce. According to Standard Chartered's Benjamin Hung, the next phase of trade will increasingly be shaped by the flow of services, in particular, in the form of knowledge, standards and ideas. "Through years of reform and opening up, China has become one of the world's leading trading nations and a major contributor to global growth and prosperity," Hung said, adding that Standard Chartered has been privileged to both witness this journey firsthand and take part in it. "We live in a world of increasing fragmentation, yet trade remains one of the few truly universal languages, connecting people, markets and opportunities across borders. Trade works best when it is open, transparent, predictable and rules-based," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China issues plan to boost strength in finance during 2026-2030 period
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
China issues plan to boost strength in finance during 2026-2030 period BEIJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- China has issued a plan to strengthen its financial sector during 2026-2030, focusing on preventing financial risks, strengthening financial supervision, and promoting high-quality development. The office of the Central Financial Commission formulated the plan in coordination with relevant financial authorities, said Lu Lei, deputy governor of the People's Bank of China (PBOC), at a press conference on Thursday. By 2030, China aims to put in place the overall framework of a modern financial system with Chinese characteristics, ensure that financial regulation policies are well coordinated and effective, optimize the structure of the financial system, ensure rigorous and effective financial supervision, and make financial risk prevention and control targeted and efficient, according to the plan. Other goals for 2030 include continued improvements in the quality and effectiveness of financial support for economic and social development, a comprehensive legal framework for the financial sector, steady expansion of high-standard financial opening up, and continued increases in the sector's international influence and competitiveness. The plan aims to largely establish a highly adaptive, competitive, and inclusive modern financial system with Chinese characteristics by 2035, laying a solid foundation for further boosting China's strength in finance. Key tasks outlined in the plan include improving the financial macro-regulation system, strengthening financial supervision, effectively preventing and defusing financial risks, serving the real economy more proactively and effectively, promoting high-quality development of the financial sector, and expanding high-standard financial opening up. MONETARY POLICY FRAMEWORK Regarding monetary policy, Lu said China will continue to transform and improve its monetary policy framework to better adapt it to the profound changes in the country's economic and financial structures. The PBOC, China's central bank, will remain firmly committed to maintaining currency value stability and thereby promoting economic growth and providing effective support for the high-quality development of the real economy. It will enhance its base money supply mechanism and reserve requirement system, and conduct open market operations with greater flexibility and precision, Lu said. China will maintain its managed floating exchange rate system, allow the market to play a decisive role in exchange rate formation, and guard against herd behavior and the self-reinforcement of irrational expectations, he said. The central bank will also improve monetary policy communication and expectations management, further develop credible, regular and institutionalized policy communication mechanisms, and make monetary policy communication easier to understand and more authoritative. A STRONGER, MORE INCLUSIVE CAPITAL MARKET China will accelerate a new round of capital market reform and opening up and strive to establish a new pattern of high-quality development and achieve marked improvements in the market's overall strength and international competitiveness by 2030, the 40th anniversary of the establishment of China's capital market, said Li Chao, vice chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, at the press conference. The securities regulator will introduce more inclusive rules for stock issuance and listings and for mergers and acquisitions, and work to make the A-share market the preferred listing venue for high-quality domestic companies, Li said. Since the beginning of the year, medium- and long-term funds, including social security funds, annuity funds and insurance funds, have purchased more than 600 billion yuan (about 88.4 billion U.S. dollars) worth of A-shares on a net basis. The market value of their holdings of tradable A-shares has increased 12.5 percent since the end of 2025, Li said. FINANCIAL STABILITY AND OPENING UP In the banking and insurance sectors, China will prudently prevent and control risks in key areas, take forceful, orderly and effective steps to prevent and defuse risks at local small and medium-sized financial institutions, and firmly guard against major risk events, said Cong Lin, deputy head of the National Financial Regulatory Administration. Financial institutions will be guided to shift from a model of scale-driven, high-speed expansion to one focused on quality and performance, while strong action will be taken against price wars, illegal commission rebates and practices involving excessively high interest rates and returns, Cong said. Cong said differentiated measures will be taken to optimize the system of financial institutions, clarify the permitted scope of business and prohibited conduct for different types of institutions, and guide them to focus on their core businesses and pursue differentiated development. These steps aim to enhance the adaptability and competitiveness of the financial system. China has achieved basic convertibility for direct investment transactions, said Li Bin, deputy head and spokesperson of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. Cross-border securities investment arrangements now include institutional investor programs, market connectivity mechanisms and direct access to domestic markets for overseas investors, while all forms of cross-border financing are subject to macro-prudential management, Li said. More broadly, during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), China's banking and insurance sectors provided more than 170 trillion yuan in additional financing support to the real economy through loans, bonds and equity, while the broader financial sector advanced reform and opening up, strengthened supervision and made progress in addressing risks in key areas, officials said at Thursday's press conference. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for accelerating the development of a modern financial system with Chinese characteristics. The plan emphasizes aligning the growth of social financing and the money supply with targets for economic growth and overall price levels, as well as increasing the flexibility of the renminbi exchange rate while maintaining its basic stability at an adaptive and balanced level. It also calls for expanding patient capital, improving the supporting system for the entry of medium- and long-term funds into the capital market, and strengthening financial supervision and the prevention and resolution of financial risks.
